idiom_name: fun interface + SAM conversion; inline reified for erased-type recovery
implementation_notes: Kotlin takes the JVM route with better ergonomics: a Kotlin-declared fun interface (1.4+) has exactly one abstract method, so a lambda or callable reference converts to it implicitly, and a richer contract is a normal interface implemented by an object expression. Generic type arguments are erased exactly as in Java, so runtime type tests need an explicit token; inline fun <reified T> reproduces the type argument inside the inlined body, allowing is T, as T and T::class without a Class parameter. Prefer a plain function type ((Int) -> Boolean) when the contract really is a function, and a fun interface (or typealias) when the API benefits from a named type, extension functions or inheritance.
code_sketch:
fun interface Renderer { fun render(value: Any): String }   // exactly one abstract method

val money = Renderer { "%,.2f".format(it as Double) }        // SAM conversion from a lambda

inline fun <reified T> Any.isA(): Boolean = this is T      // recovers the erased type argument

val items: List<Any> = listOf(1, "two")
items.filter { it.isA<String>() }                           // type argument known at compile time
pitfalls: JVM erasure applies to Kotlin generics too: is List<String> does not compile (only is List<*>), and as T inside a non-inline function is an unchecked cast that can throw where the value is used.
A fun interface with more than one abstract member can no longer be SAM-converted; adding a second abstract method breaks every lambda call site.

Kotlin calls a Kotlin fun interface directly but wraps a Java functional interface; repeated SAM conversions in hot paths allocate, so use a function type or an inline function when the difference matters.
